title: Johann Christian von Mannlich
collection: Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Neue Pinakothek München (not on display; donated 1921)
reproduction_credit: Johann Baptist Seele, Johann Christian von Mannlich, 1808, Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Neue Pinakothek München (CC BY-SA 4.0)
status_note: Museum released CC BY-SA 4.0 (licence link on the collection page). Resized to 1600 px, metadata stripped; this derivative stays CC BY-SA 4.0 with the credit above.
use: Primary face reference, age 66–67: long narrow face, long nose, brown eyes, own unpowdered hair, dark coat, high white cravat, order ribbon in the buttonhole. Only colour image of the adult Mannlich.

title: Johann Christian v. Mannlich (frontispiece)
artist: Johann Baptist Seele (painting); halftone plate in E. Stollreither (ed.), Ein deutscher Maler und Hofmann. Lebenserinnerungen des Joh. Christian v. Mannlich, Berlin: Mittler 1910
medium: oil painting (plate caption: 'Nach einem Ölgemälde'); reproduced as a halftone plate
collection: Painting then owned by Hauptmann v. Mannlich-Lehmann, Berlin (plate caption); present location unknown
reproduction_licence: Public domain: plate photo published 1910, so photo protection under §72 UrhG (50 years after publication) ended in 1960; the scan is a plain page scan
reproduction_credit: Scan: Internet Archive, digitised from a copy of the Getty Research Institute
status_note: 1910 printed reproduction. Internet Archive page scan, no rights claimed in the item metadata. Cropped to the plate and caption, resized, metadata stripped. The 1910 list of plates names Seele as painter; the editor's introduction (p. XLVIII) says Mannlich's likeness survives through this Seele painting, 'later engraved after the drawing by Hoffnaß'.
use: Second version of the Seele type (family version): same face, other light and framing

title: Johann Christian von Mannlich, 1740–1822, Selbstbildnis (title on the archive card)
artist: Card: Johann Christian von Mannlich (self-portrait). Probably the same Berlin painting the 1910 edition attributes to Seele (not verified)
collection: Berlin, von Mannlich-Lehmann (as photographed c. 1940); present location unknown
inventory_number: Foto Marburg image no. mi00233c05; bildindex obj00002580
reproduction_credit: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg (photo: Friedrich van der Smissen)
status_note: Foto Marburg marks this historic archive photo Public Domain Mark 1.0 (via Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek). Whole archive card kept, with its typed caption.
use: Same Berlin version as the 1910 plate, photographed straight: good for the profile line of nose and chin

title: Portret van Johann Christian von Mannlich
artist: Hoffnass, engraver ('Hoffnaß fec.'), after Johann Baptist Seele ('Seele pinx.'). Rijksmuseum names Johann Wilhelm Hoffnass (1727–1795); Deutsches Museum names Lorenz Hoffnass
date: after 1806 (inscription gives the royal Bavarian title, which only existed from 1806); the 1910 introduction says it was engraved later than the Seele painting
status_note: Rijksmuseum releases its images under the Public Domain Mark. Resized, metadata stripped.
use: Black-and-white line version of the Seele face. Inscription: 'J. C. von Mannlich / Director aller Königl. baierischen Kunst-Samlungen'.

title: Zeichnender Junge (Bavarian State Painting Collections title); shown in Schwarzenacker as 'Jugendporträt von J. C. Mannlich'
date: c. 1756 (per the gallery caption, as quoted on Commons)
collection: Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen (from the Zweibrücken gallery), shown in the Gemäldegalerie Schwarzenacker (Edelhaus), Homburg
status_note: Commons: photographer's own photo (2019) of the painting on the gallery wall, CC BY 4.0. Resized, metadata incl. GPS stripped. The museum's own title is neutral ('Drawing boy'); the identification with the young J. C. Mannlich (c. 15) comes from the Schwarzenacker display.
use: Youth: profile line, own brown hair tied back, brown coat. Shows him as a draughtsman by lamplight, a possible motif.

title: Mannlich, Christian von (impression of the Hoffnass engraving after Seele)
artist: Lorenz Hoffnass after Johann Baptist Seele (per record)
status_note: Not downloaded: non-commercial licence. Same print as the Rijksmuseum impression, which is stored.
use: Gives the engraver's first name as Lorenz

title: Lithographed chalk drawing of the artist and his wife
collection: Maillinger-Sammlung, München, per the 1910 introduction (the collection is today in the Münchner Stadtmuseum; the sheet itself not traced)
status_note: Known only from the 1910 introduction (p. XLVIII): 'Eine lithographierte Kreidezeichnung, die den Künstler und seine Frau darstellt, birgt die Maillinger Sammlung zu München.' Could relate to the 1778 double self-portrait below (not verified).
use: Would be the only image of him with his wife; worth a request to the Münchner Stadtmuseum

title: Selbstbildnis mit Frau (self-portrait with his wife)
status_note: Listed in the NDB article (Roland, NDB 16, 1990); location and image not found. It would be the only portrait from the Karlsberg years (he was 37).
use: Key missing image for the 1778–1793 look

title: Bust of Mannlich from his grave
status_note: Wikipedia says the bust from the grave in the Alter Südfriedhof is now in the Münchner Stadtmuseum. Not found online.
use: Would give the head in 3D (old age)

title: Statue of Mannlich in front of the Christian-von-Mannlich-Gymnasium, Homburg
artwork_licence: Modern work; check freedom of panorama before any reuse
status_note: Not stored: modern interpretation, not historical evidence.
use: Local memory of Mannlich in Homburg (codex)

title: Memorial plate for Mannlich, Alter Südfriedhof München (1972)
medium: stone plate with coat of arms, no portrait
status_note: Not stored: shows no likeness. The original grave was destroyed in the Second World War.
